Hi Sam / Priya 

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we can model a proposal that maps to your unit economics: 

Recap:
- Primary use: in-product assistant (contextual help + transaction summarization).
- Estimated steady-state token volume: 10M tokens / month (pilot: ~2M / month; expected peak 50M+ in Year 1 if adoption scales).
- Key constraints: procurement budget band $50k-$120k / month (incl. infra + platform).
- Quality requirement: <300ms median server-side generation latency for short prompts (<=512 tokens) and SLO-driven fallbacks.

Asks for us to price and build unit-econ model:
1) Confirm estimated monthly token volumes (pilot / steady / peak).
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens you'd like to aim for at scale (your procurement team asked: target $/1M tokens for the primary model).
3) Provide rough metrics per feature: monthly active users, average calls/user/month, avg tokens per call (best-effort).
4) Any CAC / payback targets or margin thresholds we should optimize for (e.g., target gross margin after inference cost, acceptable CAC payback window).

Next steps (proposed):
- You share the three items above  we' ll run the unit economics model and return a recommended pricing tier (hosted vs dedicated) and a sample per-feature pricing construct (e.g., $/active-user-month or per-1k-calls).
- If the numbers look aligned, we'll draft an SOW + pilot pricing and include optional reserved capacity and trial credits.

Attaching the initial unit economics workbook I used on today's call  it has example rows for tokens-per-call, calls per MAU, inference cost assumptions, and conversion/CAC sensitivity tabs.

Cheers,

Thanks for the context  good catch on the MAU math. A few notes and an updated recommendation (high level)  I updated the attached workbook (unit_econ_model_v2.xlsx) with two scenarios and kernel-level inference assumptions: quantized LLM baseline and mixed higher-quality variant fallback.

Quick takeaways:
- The customer-procurement target ($200-$400 / 1M tokens) is achievable for the pilot and steady volumes if we: (a) use a quantized model variant as default, (b) enable prefix caching for common prompts, and (c) offer a modest reserved-capacity discount for a 6-12 month commit.
- Recommended list pricing (per 1M input+output tokens): Hosted: $350 / 1M; Dedicated (reserved): $225 / 1M; Private (on-prem / VPC): $175 / 1M (assumes customer covers infra ops).
- Expected gross margin assumptions (post-inference cost, excluding sales/ CAC):
  - Hosted @ 10M tokens/mo: ~55% gross margin (without reserved discount).
  - Dedicated @ 10M tokens/mo with 12-mo commit: ~68% gross margin.
  - Private (customer-managed infra): ~72% gross margin for Redwood (platform fees only).

Per-feature pricing examples (mapping to FintechX numbers):
- If MAU=100k, calls/user/month=5, avg tokens/call=450 -> tokens/mo ~225M. At Dedicated list price $225/1M this implies monthly inference cost ~$50,625.
- Translate to per-MAU pricing: $50,625 / 100k MAU = $0.506 / MAU / month (inference only).
- Per-1k-calls construct: calls/mo = 100k * 5 = 500k calls; per-1k-calls price to cover inference = $50,625 / 500 = $101.25 per 1k calls (this is a high-level mapping; you can package as $X per 1k calls + platform fee).

Pilot recommendation:
- Pilot (2M tokens/mo): provide 2 months of 50% credits on Hosted list price and offer a path to convert to Dedicated with a 12-mo commit at a 30% reserved discount. Include a short SOW with success criteria (latency <350ms, 90% availability, accuracy checks on prompt set).

CAC / payback note:
- If FintechX target gross margin is >=60%, the Dedicated option with the reserved discount gets them in range and also provides a predictable unit cost for CAC payback modeling. With our suggested structure, their CAC payback at expected conversion rates looks feasible within 6-9 months (we'll finalize after they confirm MAU estimates).

I'll attach the updated workbook and a priced sample SOW. Let me know if you want me on the procurement call.

 Aditya
